clue.text: Witty talk not good during a particular period

blocks.note: the plain opposite of good
'during the war' is 'in the war'
an age is a distinct period of history

explanation.surface: Someone complains that clever conversation was in short supply in some era.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to judge the conversation of an era; 'during' quietly supplies a two-letter preposition rather than setting the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter exchanged between people, a French borrowing for light repartee.

clue.text: Shakespeare reportedly not allowed

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how something is said

blocks.note: Shakespeare is known as the Bard of Avon

explanation.surface: A rumour that Shakespeare has been banned from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare is 'the Bard'; spoken aloud, BARD and BARRED are the same in most British accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Something barred is prohibited or excluded, as a person barred from entering a pub.

clue.text: Business bigwigs here? A man gets excited

indicators.note: excited things are stirred up and agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, doing double duty as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A man gets thrilled at the sight of some powerful businesspeople.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites us to look for the bigwigs 'here', in the words that follow: A MAN GETS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnates are wealthy, influential leaders of industry, the very people informally called bigwigs.

clue.text: Girl with love ensnaring American soldier slowly

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap and hold, so one part closes around another

blocks.note: a girl's name
GI is the standard term for a US soldier
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A girl in love captures a GI's heart at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the girl to love, so both go round the soldier; only the final word is the definition, a musical tempo marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian musical direction meaning to play at a slow, easy tempo.

clue.text: Fake, a new spiritual quack

definitions.note: a sceptical description of a shaman

blocks.note: a sham is a fake
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone denounces a new religious healer as a fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fake' looks like a description of the quack, but it is the first piece, SHAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman claims healing and contact with spirits; a doubter would call such a person a fraudulent healer.

clue.text: One who cannot get out? Shame about rudimentary accommodation

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round the other

blocks.note: a sin is a shameful act
a hut is a basic shelter

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a poor shelter feels ashamed of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is playful: a shut-in is housebound, not literally locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: A shut-in is a person confined to home by illness or disability, who rarely or never ventures outside.

clue.text: Male viper in plant

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
the adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a viper

explanation.surface: A male snake lurks inside a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but nothing goes inside anything: it just joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Madder is a climbing herb whose roots were long used to make a red dye.

clue.text: Socialist with crude plan again

blocks.note: red is the traditional colour of the left
raw means unrefined, crude

explanation.surface: A left-winger with a rough scheme has to start the planning over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude plan' reads as one phrase, but 'crude' belongs to the wordplay and 'plan again' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a map or boundary is to draft it afresh, laying out a design once more.

clue.text: Time to join a composer, a fellow who organises the trip?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the person, completed by 'a fellow' in the wordplay

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
Maurice Ravel, the French composer of Bolero
taken as written
a gent is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A musician is hired to join a composer on tour, with someone arranging the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: Time, composer, a and fellow simply follow one another; 'a fellow' also completes the sense of the definition, a man who arranges trips.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel agent books flights, hotels and holidays for customers, arranging journeys professionally.

clue.text: Carriage taken across America is more crowded maybe

indicators.note: something carried across spans the other part, so it sits on both sides of it

blocks.note: a bier is the stand or carriage on which a coffin is borne
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A carriage driving across the USA gets more packed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carriage' suggests a bus, which is a trap: the carriage is the frame a coffin rides on, split around the country's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A busier place has more activity and people in it; 'maybe' admits that crowded is only one example.

clue.text: One deserting Eden with rage out of control

indicators.note: things out of control run wild and lose their order, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone storms out of paradise in an uncontrollable fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes leaving the Garden of Eden, but Eden and rage are only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade abandons a cause, party or religion, a turncoat who goes over to the other side.

clue.text: This writer's found in the French capital

indicators.note: what is found inside something sits within it

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as 'this writer'; 'writer's' = writer is = I'M
la is a French word for 'the'

explanation.surface: The author announces being in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French capital' looks like Paris, but 'the French' is LA and 'capital' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru, a seat of national government on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Religious ado, violent unfortunately

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is things going wrong, so the letters go awry into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A row over faith has sadly turned violent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious' looks like it describes the fuss, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotional writing or music is used in worship and prayer, so it is pious in purpose.

clue.text: Hater's yells, terrible, lacking any compassion

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase describing how something is done

indicators.note: something terrible is in a dreadful state, so the letters are left in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone full of hate screams awful abuse with no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'Hater's' is ignored, as crossword punctuation usually may be.
explanation.definitionFit: To act heartlessly is to behave cruelly, without pity or sympathy for others.

clue.text: Artist in autumn shows weather phenomenon

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
taken as written
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painter at work in autumn captures some typical weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal, but putting the artist inside the season gives nonsense; the little word supplies its own two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainfall is precipitation, water dropping from clouds, a standard item in any weather report.

clue.text: Tear apart material with speed

blocks.note: lace is a delicate fabric
rate is speed, as in 'at a fast rate'

explanation.surface: Someone rips cloth to pieces in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear apart material' reads as one action, but 'material' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to rip or gash flesh or fabric, leaving a jagged wound or tear.

clue.text: Modern culture has endless requirement to accommodate witty person

indicators.note: something without an end has lost its final letter
to accommodate is to house a guest, so one part takes another inside

blocks.note: NEED, a requirement, minus its last letter
a wag is a joker

explanation.surface: Contemporary culture always needs a comedian or two to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion happens first, then the shortened word plays host, splitting after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age describes a modern movement of alternative spirituality, holistic health and astrology that grew from the 1970s.

clue.text: Way in which mister entertains king's sister

indicators.note: a host entertains guests in the home, so one part holds another

blocks.note: Mr is the abbreviation for mister
Princess Anne is the sister of King Charles III

explanation.surface: A gentleman hosts royalty and shows how it should be done.
explanation.walkthrough: MR opens up to hold ANNE; 'in which' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is the method or style in which something is done, as in 'in this manner'.

clue.text: Dull person in the belfry or someone similar

blocks.note: first meaning, playful: a lifeless, boring bell-ringer
second meaning: a person who looks exactly like another

explanation.surface: A tedious bell-ringer up in the tower, or someone just like them.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a whimsical reading: 'dead' as dull, a 'ringer' as one who rings bells in a belfry.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an exact double; separately, a ringer is literally one who rings church bells.

clue.text: Beer stocked by the German shopkeeper?

indicators.note: goods stocked by a shop are held inside it, so one part sits within another

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A German shopkeeper keeps beer on the shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The German shopkeeper' reads as one person, but 'the German' is DER. The question mark admits a dealer need not have a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer buys and sells goods, like a trader running a business selling antiques or cars.

clue.text: Noisy goings-on outside a show

indicators.note: one part stands on the outer side of the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: a revel is a boisterous celebration
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rowdy behaviour breaks out outside a theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun for a performance, but it is the verb, meaning to display.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to uncover or disclose it, letting others see it.

clue.text: Talk a short time after church

indicators.note: something coming after follows behind, setting the order of the parts

blocks.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A brief conversation once the service ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' signals the abbreviation of time to T rather than a deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal conversation, the casual speaking people do over coffee.

clue.text: Fuel gets fliers flying initially when in distress

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is taken
being inside something places one part within the other

blocks.note: pain is suffering, distress
the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's fliers
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fuel supply rescues aircrew in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Air Force are the crossword's usual 'fliers'; 'when in distress' looks like a rescue scenario but marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for kerosene, an oil burnt in lamps and heaters.

clue.text: Singer Lynn keeps performing in Italian city

indicators.note: to keep is to hold on to, so one part is held inside another

blocks.note: Dame Vera Lynn, the British wartime singer of 'We'll Meet Again'
a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: Vera Lynn is still singing on tour in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Vera Lynn, famous for songs cheering British troops in the Second World War, gives VERA, holding ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Verona is a city in northern Italy, the setting of Romeo and Juliet.

clue.text: Archdeacon in cathedral city regularly

indicators.note: being in something places one part inside the other

blocks.note: an archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', abbreviated Ven
Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: An archdeacon regularly turns up in a cathedral city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' suggests taking alternate letters, but here it is the definition. ELY is the crossword's favourite cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means in a uniform, steady way, with equal spacing, just as regularly does.

clue.text: Ride through African territory

indicators.note: the answer runs right through the following words, spanning their boundary

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Someone goes on horseback across a stretch of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in afriCAN TERritory; 'through' seems part of the journey but signals the concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A canter is a horse's easy three-beat pace, so to go for a canter is a ride.
